title: A New Population of Jovian Exoplanets Suitable For Direct Imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, the Roman Coronagraph, and ELTs Identified from HARPS Radial-Velocity Data and Hipparcos-Gaia A
byline: Li; Jie; Currie; Thayne; Yiting; Morsy; Mona El; Lubin; Jack; Bovie; Danielle; Lujan; Nathaniel; Dykes; Erica
html:
Abstract:We jointly analyze archival radial-velocity data from the HARPS spectrograph and astrometry from Hipparcos and Gaia to identify and constrain the dynamical properties of new and known long-period jovian exoplanets. Our search yields 14 new confirmed planets with masses of 0.04--6.1 $M_{\rm Jup}$ and semimajor axes of 0.1--12.6 au. Planets include a super-Jupiter in a near-Saturn-like orbit producing a strong astrometric acceleration (HIP 669 b), an eccentric Jupiter around a K star with a modest acceleration (HIP 39039 b), a 74-day-orbit warm Neptune (HIP 64550 b), and a giant planet around a Tier A Habitable Worlds Observatory target that may endanger any habitable zone Earth (HIP 17378 b). Three systems show evidence for candidate planets requiring additional data for confirmation. Our modeling also constrains the dynamical masses and orbits for 32 previously known radial-velocity-discovered planets.
Orbits, masses, and ages for our sample show that five targets are potentially detectable in reflected light with the Roman Coronagraph, 28 should be imageable in reflected light with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, and six may be detectable in thermal emission with E-ELT/METIS. These results demonstrate the power of combining archival radial-velocity data with astrometry to discover and characterize long-period giant planets, a capability that will only grow with Gaia DR4. It provides a new sample of targets for future direct-imaging observations, and shows a path forward for timely vetting of targets for exo-Earth imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory.
